title: 2026-10-22_Fancy_Bear_Incident_Response_aec
description: Investigate and respond to a potential cyber espionage activity attributed to the Fancy Bear threat group.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected potential cyber espionage activity attributed to the Fancy Bear threat group. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. The compromised host is `target` (192.168.50.5) with credentials: username `cyrano`, password `cyrano`.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox in cloud using the following credentials: username `cyrano`, password `cyrano`. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: Access the local sandbox using the following credentials: username `cyrano`, password `cyrano`. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: While monitoring network traffic, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate this activity and identify the suspicious service responsible for these connections. Submit the service name as your answer.
levels.solution: Check running services and their network connections. The suspicious service is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by examining the list of running services on the system.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Focus on services that have active network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all services with network connections.

levels.title: Analyze Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Now that you've identified the suspicious service, determine how it maintains persistence on the system. Investigate the persistence mechanism used by this service. Submit the persistence identifier as your answer.
levels.solution: Check systemd services and their configurations. The persistence identifier is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Begin by examining the systemd service configurations.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are set to start automatically at boot.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled` to list all enabled services.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Examine the host for evidence of lateral movement. Identify any scripts or services that might be transferring data to other hosts in the network. Submit the script name as your answer.
levels.solution: Check for scheduled tasks and transfer scripts. The script name is `payload-transfer.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by checking the cron jobs and scheduled tasks.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for scripts that are set to run at regular intervals.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `crontab -l` to list all scheduled tasks for the current user.
